title: Lex Kratom — 21+ age limit, distance-sales ban, excise stamp and 21% VAT on kratom from 2027
money_note: No spending is attached. The finance ministry estimates first-year tax revenue of about 0.5bn CZK (0.3bn excise, 0.2bn VAT); that is a fiscal yield, not a budget for the need, so it is not scored as money.
summary: The government approved on 14 September 2026 an amendment to Act 167/1998 on addictive substances and eight related acts that raises the purchase age for psychomodulatory substances such as kratom from 18 to 21, bans internet and other distance sales, tightens shop, composition, labelling and batch-control rules, and adds a kratom excise tax of 2 to 20 CZK per gram with mandatory tax stamps and a move from 12 to 21 percent VAT. The bill also brings nicotine pouches under an e-cigarette-style product regime and bans selling technical-hemp flower to individuals; it takes effect on 1 January 2027 with a five-month adaptation period.
notes: STATUS: DRAFT — government bill approved by the government on 14 September 2026 (VeKLEP material KORNDVEC8EF8, stav '9 - projednano', version for the government meeting authorised 2026-09-01; out of the legislative plan, 'Z duvodu ochrany verejneho zdravi'), now heading to the Chamber. DATES: proposed effect 1 January 2027 (Cl. on ucinnost: 'Tento zakon nabyva ucinnosti dnem 1. ledna 2027'); sellers must adapt to the new conditions within 5 months of effect; existing psychomodulatory-substance permit holders are treated as kratom tax-warehouse holders for 1 month and must apply within 1 month; unstamped stock may be sold for 5 months. Excise rates per the MF/MZd press release of 14 Sep 2026: 2 CZK/g or ml for ordinary kratom, 10 CZK for concentrates, 20 CZK for illegal (unstamped) kratom. Same-day related step: the government backed MPs' bill snemovni tisk 297 (VeKLEP KORNDXPG8PUE, surfaced by the scripted feed as veklep-KORNDXPG8PUE on 2026-09-08) letting the police close a shop for up to 14 days where a product posing a serious risk to life or health is handled, with 48 hours for the supervisory body to confirm; its effect is the first day of the second month after promulgation, so it carries no fixed date. Sources: MZd press release https://mzd.gov.cz/tiskove-centrum-mz/vlada-schvalila-lex-kratom-ministerstva-zdravotnictvi-a-financi-zprisnuji-regulaci-kratomu-i-dalsich-rizikovych-vyrobku/ ; vlada.gov.cz 14 Sep 2026 meeting summary. DEDUP: the scripted veklep feed already holds this material as veklep-KORNDVEC8EF8 (metadata only); this record is the dated substance of the approved bill and does not re-mint that id. Act 270/2025 (reg-cz-psilocybin-2026, reg-detsky-certifikat-2027) is a different act. Who must act: kratom and psychomodulatory-substance shops and distributors, e-shops that sell them today, nicotine-pouch makers, importers and retailers, municipalities (new power to regulate shop locations by ordinance).
quote: (5) Prodejce je povinen zajistit, že v okamžiku prodeje psychomodulačních látek dojde k ověření, že kupující osoba není mladší 21 let.

title: Zákon o inovativním a škálovatelném podnikání — startup register and investor tax deduction from July 2027
money_note: Lower bound of the RIA's own estimate of annual public-budget cost, 65-75 million CZK in the low scenario up to 193-201 million CZK in the high scenario, converted at 24.5 CZK/EUR (65,000,000 / 24.5).
summary: The industry ministry's draft startup act, in inter-ministerial comment procedure since 15 September 2026, creates an electronic register of 'rozvijejici se podniky' kept by Agentura CzechBusiness (limited or joint-stock companies under 8 years old, 10 in long-cycle sectors, with turnover up to 250 million CZK) and lets early-stage investors deduct qualifying risk investments of up to 5 million CZK a year from their tax base, carried forward five years, with longer loss carry-forward for registered firms. It is planned to take effect on 1 July 2027, and its RIA names the problem as the low number of innovative startups that are founded and survive in Czechia.
notes: STATUS: DRAFT — MPO bill in comment procedure (VeKLEP ALBSDXTKB4NK authorised 2026-09-15, comments due 2026-10-14; re-posted as KORNDXY8B5OY on 2026-09-16, comments due 2026-10-15), submitted under government resolution 175/2026 (legislative plan). DATES: proposed effect 1 July 2027 ('Tento zakon nabyva ucinnosti dnem 1. cervence 2027', materiál https://www.odok.cz/portal/services/download/attachment/KORNDXXJ4SDO/). RIA 'Definice problemu' cites Dealroom 2025: 972 startups with external investment founded since 2015 (89.2 per million inhabitants) against Estonia's 681 per million, and VC investment of 25 USD per capita in 2024. Registration conditions in section 3 of the draft; deduction in the new section 15d of the income tax act (max 5,000,000 CZK per period, pro rata above that); administrative offences fined 100,000-500,000 CZK. DEDUP: reg-startupy-zakon (2026-08-14 ledger) records the plan item MPO-17 as a pre-draft with planned effect January 2028; this record is the published draft, which dates effect six months EARLIER, 1 July 2027, and states the instruments. Neither veklep PID is in seen.txt (the scripted feed has not run since 2026-09-08). Who must act: startups seeking the status, angel and early-stage investors, Agentura CzechBusiness (new register), tax advisers.

title: eTurista — national accommodation register and STR single digital entry point, now dated 1 January 2028
money_note: The RIA quantifies public and private costs in its section 3 but no single appropriation for the register is stated in the material read; nothing is estimated.
summary: The regional-development ministry's amendment to Tourism Act 159/1999, in comment procedure since 14 September 2026, creates eTurista, a public register of accommodation facilities and short-term-rental units that becomes Czechia's single digital entry point under EU Regulation 2024/1028 and lets one data entry satisfy the foreigner-registration, statistics, trade-licence and local-fee reporting duties that hosts now file separately. The draft sets effect for 1 January 2028, a year later than the 01.2027 the legislative plan and the RIA's own header originally carried.
notes: STATUS: DRAFT — VeKLEP ALBSDXWJ7VQX, 'v pripominkovem rizeni', authorised 2026-09-14, comments due 2026-10-13; legislative plan item MMR-1. DATES: proposed effect 1 January 2028 ('Tento zakon nabyva ucinnosti dnem 1. ledna 2028', materiál https://www.odok.cz/portal/services/download/attachment/ALBSDXWLCP2Z/); the RIA header shows the planned effect moved 01.27 -> 01.28. EU link: Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 has applied since 20 May 2026 (reg-str-registration); the RIA notes no transposition deadline because a registration scheme is a member-state choice. Scale per the RIA: CSU counted 10,012 collective accommodation establishments with 217,701 rooms and 562,467 beds in 2025, and says the true number is much higher. RIA problem areas: duplicate reporting burden on hosts, missing visitor and host data, unequal conditions and grey economy. DEDUP: reg-str-registr-pronajmu (plan item, effect 1 Jan 2027) and reg-str-registration (the EU regulation) already exist; this record is the published draft and its CHANGED date, stated so the register's 2027 date is not relied on. Who must act: hotels, pensions, private hosts, platforms (Airbnb, Booking) connecting to the entry point, municipalities collecting the accommodation fee, foreign police.

title: Forced Labour Regulation, Czech enforcement — labour inspectorate, market surveillance and customs, fines to 5 million CZK
money_note: No budget is attached; the 5,000,000 CZK figure is a maximum fine, not money attached to the need.
summary: The industry ministry's draft amendment to Act 151/2021 on special foreign-trade regimes and Act 251/2005 on labour inspection, in comment procedure since 10 September 2026, adapts Czech law to EU Forced Labour Regulation 2024/3015: labour-inspection bodies investigate forced labour on Czech territory, market-surveillance authorities open investigations and issue product decisions on the inspectorate's binding opinion, customs checks goods entering the market, and a new section 6a sets fines up to 5 million CZK. It is to take effect on 14 December 2027, the regulation's general application date.
notes: STATUS: DRAFT — VeKLEP KORNDXQH4G02, 'v pripominkovem rizeni', authorised 2026-09-10, comments due 2026-10-09 (reason given: adaptation of the Czech legal order to Regulation (EU) 2024/3015). DATES: proposed effect 14 December 2027 ('Tento zakon nabyva ucinnosti dnem 14. prosince 2027', materiál https://www.odok.cz/portal/services/download/attachment/ALBSDXSFUJBT/, CELEX 32024R3015); the regulation applies generally from 14 December 2027 with some provisions earlier, and member states must notify their penalty rules under Art 37(3). Fine: 'Za prestupek podle odstavce 1 lze ulozit pokutu do vyse 5 000 000 Kc' (section 6a). The customs administration is to pass EORI identifiers of importers to the ministry. DEDUP: reg-forced-labour (2026-08-13) records the EU regulation and its 14 Dec 2027 date from law-firm commentary; this record is the Czech enforcement bill (named authorities, sanctions), a distinct instrument. Who must act: every economic operator placing products on or exporting from the EU market, especially importers in automotive, electronics and textiles; SUIP and the 8 regional labour inspectorates; customs.

title: Nařízení vlády 164/2026 Sb. — minimum-wage coefficients 0.446 (2027) and 0.458 (2028) now in force
money_note: No aggregate wage-bill figure is published. The binding inputs are published: coefficient 0.446 (164/2026 Sb.) times the finance ministry's predicted 2027 average gross monthly wage of 55,627 CZK (150/2026 Sb.), which is 24,809.64 CZK before the labour code's rounding.
summary: Government regulation 164/2026 Sb. of 7 September 2026, promulgated on 15 September and in force from 16 September 2026, fixes the minimum-wage coefficient at 0.446 for 2027 and 0.458 for 2028, and finance-ministry notice 150/2026 Sb. of 18 August 2026 sets the predicted 2027 average gross monthly wage at 55,627 CZK. Under section 111 of the labour code the product of the two is the monthly minimum wage every employer must pay from 1 January 2027.
notes: STATUS: ENACTED — 164/2026 Sb. (nařízení vlády ze dne 7. září 2026, ELI versions 2026-09-15 promulgated / 2026-09-16 in force) and 150/2026 Sb. (sdělení MF ze dne 18. srpna 2026). Read from the e-Sbirka ELI open-data endpoint (opendata.eselpoint.gov.cz, text fragments). DATES: in force 16 Sep 2026; applies to wages from 1 Jan 2027 (coefficient 0.446) and 1 Jan 2028 (0.458); statutory glide path to 47 percent by 2029. DEDUP: reg-min-mzda-koeficient-2027-2028 (2026-09-03 ledger) recorded the PROPOSAL from the MPSV press release of 18 June 2026, and veklep-KORNDV4MNCNT holds the draft's metadata; this record is the ENACTMENT (Sbirka numbers, in-force date) plus the published wage prediction that turns the coefficient into a crown amount. Knock-on: the lowest public-sector pay tariff is to be tied to the minimum wage (platform-work transposition bill awaiting first reading, per the tripartite press conference of 17 Sep 2026). Who must act: every employer (payroll reconfiguration each January), OSVC and OBZP health-insurance minimums keyed to it.

title: Zákon 152/2026 Sb. — superdávka housing norm moves from municipality size to district from October 2026
money_note: The act states no appropriation and no cost figure; nothing is estimated.
summary: Act 152/2026 Sb. of 29 July 2026 amends the state social assistance benefit act 151/2025 so that from 1 October 2026 the normative rent behind the housing component of the single benefit (superdavka) is set per district rather than per municipality-size category, with new floors so a larger household never gets a lower norm than a smaller one, and MPSV must publish the district norms by notice. Its amendment to the state social support act on the parental allowance takes effect on 1 January 2027.
notes: STATUS: ENACTED — 152/2026 Sb., ELI versions 2026-08-26 (promulgated), 2026-10-01 and 2027-01-01; read from the e-Sbirka ELI open-data text fragments. DATES: Cl. VI — parts III-V (dávka státní sociální pomoci) effective 1 October 2026, the rest 1 January 2027; transitional provisions: the October 2026 benefit month is the first decided under the new rules, pending September claims finish under the old ones, and for October-December 2026 the ownership lump sum uses the norms MPSV announces. Also: the 7-day threshold in section 7(1)(e) becomes 15 days. DEDUP: reg-superdavka-prechod covers the benefit's introduction and transition; this is a later parameter change with its own dates. Who must act: MPSV and Urad prace (district norm tables, benefit IT), recipients and landlords in high-rent districts, social-housing and benefit-advice services.
quote: Tento zákon nabývá účinnosti dnem 1. ledna 2027, s výjimkou ustanovení čl. III až V, která nabývají účinnosti dnem 1. října 2026.

title: EUDR product list rewrite — soluble coffee, palm oleochemicals and soap in scope from 30 Dec 2027
money_note: The act states no EUR figure; not estimated.
summary: Delegated Regulation 2026/2102 (in force 18 Sep 2026) rewrites the EUDR product list: from 30 Dec 2027 frozen cattle tongues, soluble coffee and a set of palm-oil-derived oleochemicals, soaps, chemical preparations and polyethers become subject to deforestation due diligence. It also takes cattle hides and leather, conveyor belts and other vulcanised-rubber articles, retreaded and used tyres, sowing soya, vehicle and aircraft seats, used and second-hand goods, waste, samples and accompanying packaging out of scope with immediate effect.
notes:
- Status: ENACTED — Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/2102 of 13 July 2026, published OJ L 17 Sep 2026, in force 18 Sep 2026 (Art 2, day after publication). Each added entry carries its own clause '(This provision shall apply from 30 December 2027)'; deletions and clarifications carry no deferral, so they bite from 18 Sep 2026, i.e. before the EUDR itself applies (30 Dec 2026 large/medium, 30 Jun 2027 micro/small per reg-eudr-deforestation). Recital 21 gives the deferral as time to adapt to the new product categories.
- ADDED from 2027-12-30 (Annex points 6(b),(e),(g),(i),(k),(n),(s)): ex 0206 21 00 frozen cattle tongues; 2101 11 00 extracts, essences and concentrates of coffee (soluble coffee); ex 1516 20 hydrogenated/inter-esterified palm, palm-kernel and babassu oils; ex 1518 00 chemically modified palm oils and inedible fat mixtures made using oil palm; ex 1520 00 crude glycerol produced using oil palm; ex 2905 16 octanol; ex 2905 17 00 lauryl, cetyl and stearyl alcohol; ex 2905 19 00 other saturated monohydric alcohols; ex 2915 39 esters of acetic acid; ex 2916 15 oleic, linoleic, linolenic acids and their salts/esters; ex 2916 19 10 undecenoic acids; ex 2921 19 acyclic monoamines; ex 2923 90 00 quaternary ammonium salts; ex 2924 19 00 acyclic amides; ex 3401 11 00 toilet soap bars; ex 3401 20 soap in other forms; ex 3824 99 other chemical preparations containing or made using oil palm; ex 3907 29 other polyethers made using oil palm. The chemical entries apply only where synthesised/made using oil palm, and eight of the eighteen added entries exclude products used in manufacturing human or veterinary medicinal products. Drafting note: for ex 1520 00 the '(This provision shall apply from 30 December 2027)' clause sits after the closing quotation mark in the OJ text.
- REMOVED from 2026-09-18: ex 4101, ex 4104, ex 4107 cattle hides, skins and leather (recital 5; to be re-examined in the 2030 review under Art 34(2)); ex 4010 conveyor/transmission belts; ex 4016 other vulcanised-rubber articles; ex 4012 narrowed to 4012 90 30 tyre treads (retreaded and used tyres out); 1201 narrowed to 1201 90 00 (soya for sowing out); ex 9401 replaced by a list of wooden seats (aircraft 9401 10 00 and motor-vehicle 9401 20 00 seats out).
- NARROWED/CLARIFIED from 2026-09-18: cattle = genus Bos only (buffalo, bison out); oil palm = Elaeis only (babassu out); rubber = Hevea brasiliensis only (synthetic rubber out); wood excludes bamboo, rattan and other woody materials; existing palm-derivative codes (ex 2905 45 glycerol, ex 2915 70, ex 2915 90, ex 3823 11 00, ex 3823 12 00, ex 3823 19, ex 3823 70 00) now apply only where synthesised using oil palm; waste excluded for cocoa waste, palm oils and many wood, rubber, pulp and paper codes, and used and second-hand products excluded across many wood, rubber, pulp and paper codes; samples and products for examination/testing excluded; single-use and reusable packaging carrying another product excluded; items of correspondence and accompanying marketing material excluded.
- Dedup: related reg-eudr-deforestation (application dates 30 Dec 2026 / 30 Jun 2027 for the existing Annex I). Not a duplicate: a new act with a new scope and a new application date (30 Dec 2027) for products not previously covered. The removals also change what reg-eudr-deforestation's 30 Dec 2026 duty covers; its notes may want a line. Grep of data/signals for '2026/2102', 'soluble coffee', 'oleochemical' returned zero.
- Who must act: operators and traders placing on the EU market or exporting soluble coffee, palm-derived oleochemicals (fatty alcohols, fatty acids and esters, amines, quats, amides, glycerol), soaps and palm-based chemical preparations — detergent, cosmetics, lubricant, paint and food-additive supply chains (recital 8). Because scope turns on whether a product was made using oil palm, operators need feedstock-origin evidence to know whether a code is in scope before filing due-diligence statements with plot geolocation.
- Source read: full English text via CELLAR (celex 32026R2102), saved as data/raw/2026-09-18/regulation/eu/32026R2102-en.html.

title: Issuer-sponsored research — EU code of conduct binds investment firms
money_note: The act states no EUR figure; its 5 % threshold is a share of the research provider's revenue, not a cost. Not estimated.
summary: Delegated Regulation 2026/1092 (Listing Act RTS under MiFID II Art 24(3c)), in force since 7 Sep 2026, sets the EU code of conduct that research paid for by an issuer must meet to carry the 'issuer-sponsored research' label. Investment firms must obtain enough information from research providers to verify compliance and must not distribute research under that label when they cannot; the stated aim is to revive research coverage of SMEs.
notes:
- Status: ENACTED — Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1092 of 21 May 2026, published OJ L 4 Sep 2026, in force 7 Sep 2026 (Art 3, third day after publication). No deferred application: the duties apply now.
- Duties (Art 2): investment firms obtain from research providers all information needed to assess compliance with the code; if insufficient, they must not distribute the research labelled 'issuer-sponsored research'; they may rely on an independent third party's opinion (recital 4 names an external auditor) or on the provider's status as a MiFID investment firm, but stay responsible under MiFID II Art 24(3a), (3b), (3e).
- Code (Annex) on providers: 'issuer-sponsored research' and code compliance stated on the front page; disclosure whether the issuer paid in full or in part; disclosure where issuer-related revenue exceeds 5 % of the provider's (or third-party analyst's) consolidated gross revenues in the previous financial year; disclosure of any client or contractual relationship with the issuer in the prior 12 months, including liquidity provision; an issuer that pays in full must make the research accessible to the public free of charge; best-efforts updates after material events, with relabelling to 'marketing communication' in defined cases. ESMA based the draft on the French code (recital 7).
- Dedup: grep of data/signals for 'issuer-sponsored', 'Listing Act', '2026/1092' returned zero; no existing record.
- Why it matters / who must act: brokers and investment firms that distribute research (CNB-supervised in CZ), independent research houses and analysts, and SME issuers on EU regulated markets and SME growth markets that pay for coverage. Creates work in provider-side conflict-of-interest disclosures, firm-side verification files, and third-party compliance opinions.
- Source read: full English text via CELLAR (celex 32026R1092), saved as data/raw/2026-09-18/regulation/eu/32026R1092-en.html.
quote: Investment firms shall obtain from research providers all the information necessary to assess whether research labelled as ‘issuer-sponsored research’ is produced in compliance with the EU code of conduct set out in the Annex.

title: FRTB market-risk capital rules apply 1 Jan 2027 — relief and multipliers to 2029
money_note: The act states no EUR figure; the 0,9 and bank-specific multipliers scale capital requirements, they are not amounts. Not estimated.
summary: Delegated Regulation 2026/1221 confirms that the CRR3 (FRTB) own-funds requirements for market risk start to apply on 1 Jan 2027 and inserts transitional Articles 495i-495v running to 31 Dec 2029: a 0,9 multiplier on the standardised approaches, relaxed P&L-attribution and non-modellable-risk-factor tests, CIU look-through relief and an optional bank-specific multiplier. A bank that opts for that multiplier must recalibrate it every three months against the pre-CRR3 calculation, keep reporting market risk under the old rules, notify its supervisor and disclose the choice.
notes:
- Status: ENACTED — Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1221 of 4 June 2026, published OJ L 11 Sep 2026, in force 12 Sep 2026, applies from 1 Jan 2027 (Art 2), aligned with the start of the Regulation (EU) 2024/1623 market-risk requirements (recital 21). All transitional measures end 31 Dec 2029 (recital 4, the maximum period under CRR Art 461a(2)).
- The Commission had twice deferred FRTB by delegated act (recital 2); this act does not defer again but lowers the impact, stating it is highly unlikely that major non-EU banks will have to implement FRTB from 1 Jan 2027 (recital 17).
- Measures: Art 495i AIMA for desks failing the P&L attribution test; 495j risk factor modellable with two verifiable prices; 495k prorated observations for new issuances; 495l zero PD for 0 % risk-weight sovereigns in the default-risk model; 495m 12-week averaging and disclosure instead of 60 business days; 495n-495o CIU look-through relief; 495p zero residual-risk add-on for three named instrument types (future realised volatility, finite-date exercise options, CMS-spread options); 495q maturity assignment for equity hedges in standardised default risk; 495r EU ETS carbon correlation; 495s 0,9 multiplier on the sensitivities-based method and the simplified standardised approach; 495t ACTP index treatment; 495u small-trading-book (Art 94) institutions may use the simplified standardised approach for FX/commodity risk in the non-trading book; 495v optional bank-specific multiplier.
- Art 495v duties for banks that opt in: compare CRR3 (version in force 9 Jul 2024, with transitional treatments, as of 31 Mar 2027) against the pre-CRR3 version (8 Jul 2024); notify the competent authority without delay with evidence; recalibrate every three months; keep reporting and disclosing market-risk own funds under the 8 Jul 2024 rules; once stopped it cannot be restarted.
- Dedup: related reg-crr3-oprisk-business-indicator (CRR3 operational-risk business indicator, 23 Sep 2026). Not a duplicate: different risk pillar (market risk), different act, different date. Grep of data/signals for 'FRTB', 'market risk', '2026/1221' returned zero.
- Who must act: every EU credit institution calculating own funds for market risk (in CZ supervised by the CNB, or the ECB for significant banks). Work created: FRTB standardised-approach engines, dual-regime calculation and reporting for multiplier users, quarterly calibration, and non-modellable-risk-factor data, where recital 6 notes that third-party vendor data solutions remain limited.
- Source read: full English text via CELLAR (celex 32026R1221), saved as data/raw/2026-09-18/regulation/eu/32026R1221-en.html.
quote: The market risk requirements laid down in Regulation (EU) 2024/1623 will start to apply as of 1 January 2027. To avoid conflicting requirements for institutions, it is therefore necessary to align the date of application of this Regulation with that date.

title: Dogs and cats welfare and traceability — EU regulation phases in from 31 Aug 2028
money_note: The act states no EUR figure; not estimated.
summary: Regulation (EU) 2026/1818, in force since 30 Aug 2026, sets EU-wide welfare rules for anyone who breeds, sells, shelters or fosters dogs and cats and places them on the market, and makes microchipping plus registration in interoperable national databases mandatory. Duties phase in from 31 Aug 2028 (general welfare, registration of establishments, online-advert warnings) through 2030 (microchip and database registration for sellers), 2031 (verification tokens in online ads, platform duties, housing, import conditions) and 2034 (approval of larger breeding establishments).
notes:
- Status: ENACTED — Regulation (EU) 2026/1818 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 June 2026, published OJ L 10 Aug 2026, in force 30 Aug 2026 (Art 33: twentieth day after publication). Directly applicable; Member States may keep stricter national rules but must notify existing ones by 31 Aug 2028 (Art 30(2)).
- Duty-holders: 'operators' = anyone who places dogs or cats on the market and runs a breeding establishment, selling establishment (incl. pet shops and households), shelter, or foster placement (Art 4). 'Placing on the market' includes free transfers and advertising. Reduced duty sets for breeders with at most two litters a year and shelters with at most 15 animals or foster homes (Art 5).
- Application dates (Art 33 unless stated):
  - 31 Aug 2028 (general): welfare principles and obligations (Arts 6-7), inbreeding and hybrid ban (Art 8(4)), notification/registration of every establishment with the competent authority (Art 9), written responsible-ownership and health-history information to acquirers (Art 11), feeding (Art 14), behavioural needs (Art 17), painful practices (Art 18), shows (Art 19), mandatory warning text in online ads by operators and a responsible-ownership warning by private advertisers (Art 21(1)-(2)).
  - 31 Aug 2029: health duties, incl. daily inspection, parasite control and vaccination (Art 16); first veterinary advisory welfare visit to each establishment due by this date (Art 13(1)(a)).
  - 1 Jul 2030: no breeding from animals with excessive conformational traits (Art 8(2)); delegated act defining the traits due by 30 Jun 2030.
  - 31 Aug 2030: microchip identification and database registration for operators and anyone placing dogs or cats on the market (Art 20(7)(a)), with chipping within three months of birth or 30 days of arrival and before sale, and registration by a vet within two working days (Art 20(2)-(3)); proof of identification/registration and species, sex, date and country of birth and breed given to the acquirer (Art 21(3)); Member State registration databases (Art 23(1)).
  - 31 Aug 2031: unique verification token plus weblink to the Commission's online verification system in every online advert (Art 21(3) second subpara, 21(5)); online platforms must design their interface to facilitate those duties and tell acquirers they can verify, in line with DSA Art 31 (Art 21(4)); database interoperability and the Commission index database (Art 23(3)-(4)); housing requirements (Art 15); import conditions for dogs and cats brought in to be placed on the market, including chipping before entry and registration within five working days (Art 26(1)-(3)); competent authorities' training and certification of carers (Art 22(1)(a)-(c)).
  - 31 Aug 2033: at least one carer per establishment has completed an approved training course; competences must be documented (Art 12(2)-(3)).
  - 31 Aug 2034: approval by the competent authority, after an on-site inspection, before placing on the market for breeding establishments producing more than five litters a year or keeping more than five bitches or queens (Art 10).
  - 31 Aug 2036: pre-notification of non-commercial pet entry to the Union pet traveller database (Art 26(4)); microchipping for private dog owners (Art 20(7)(b)); genotype breeding rule (Art 8(1), from 1 Jul 2036).
  - 31 Aug 2041: microchipping for private cat owners (Art 20(7)(c)).
- Commission implementing acts on proof of registration and database content are due by 31 Aug 2028; the verification system and database interoperability acts are due by 31 Aug 2029 (Arts 21(6), 23(4)). Microchips implanted before 31 Aug 2028 under Union or national law remain compliant if still readable (Art 20(2)).
- Dedup: grep of data/signals for '2026/1818', 'dogs and cats', 'psů a koček' returned zero; no existing record. The date is 2028-08-31, the earliest application date that binds businesses (general application, Art 33).
- Why it matters: breeders, pet shops, shelters and rescues, classified-ad and marketplace platforms, veterinarians (chipping, registration, advisory visits) and national pet-database operators all get new, staggered duties; the online-ad verification token (2031) links every advert to a registered microchip.

title: End-of-life vehicles regulation — EPR, dismantling and used-car export rules from 2028
money_note: The act states no EUR figure; not estimated.
summary: Regulation (EU) 2026/1738 on vehicle circularity and end-of-life vehicles, in force since 13 Aug 2026, replaces the ELV Directive from 1 Sep 2028 and phases in duties by duty-holder. Treatment-facility and used-vehicle transfer rules come first (2028), then producer EPR, manufacturer circularity strategies, dismantling information, part removal before shredding and used-part labelling (2029), heavier vehicles and export controls (2031), and recycled-plastic content and a Digital Circularity Vehicle Passport for new types (2032).
notes:
- Status: ENACTED — Regulation (EU) 2026/1738 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 July 2026, published OJ L 24 Jul 2026, in force 13 Aug 2026 (Art 59(1)). General application 1 Sep 2028 (Art 59(2)), when Directive 2000/53/EC is repealed, with parts of it kept to 2029-2032 (Art 57(1)). Directive 2005/64/EC is repealed 31 Aug 2032 (Art 57(2)). Directly applicable; no transposition.
- Staggered dates by duty-holder:
  - 13 Aug 2026: restrictions on cadmium, lead and hexavalent chromium in batteries in M1/N1 vehicles move into Annex I of the Battery Regulation 2023/1542 (Art 53, Annex XII; Art 59(2)). The matching ELV Directive Annex II entries 5(a), 5(b)(i), 5(b)(ii) and 16 cease the same day (Art 57(1)(a)). The 12 V and 24 V SLI lead exemptions carry over, to be reviewed in 2030. This relocates existing battery rules rather than adding a new duty.
  - 1 Sep 2028 (general application; M1 and N1 cars and vans, Art 2): authorised treatment facilities accept and treat per permit and treat each end-of-life vehicle within 12 months of delivery, keeping electronic treatment records for three years (Art 26). Producer collection systems (Art 23), delivery (Art 24) and the certificate of destruction (Art 25) carry no separate date. Economic operators selling a used vehicle in the EU, including via auctions, distance contracts or online platforms, must show documentation that it is not an end-of-life vehicle, i.e. roadworthiness or an Annex I assessment (Art 36).
  - 1 Sep 2029: producer EPR, including for vehicles already made available in another Member State, so importers placing a used vehicle on a Member State's market for the first time are covered (Art 16(1)). Member State producer registers are due by 31 Aug 2029 (Art 19). Each manufacturer must draw up a circularity strategy (Art 9). Manufacturers must give waste operators, repairers and technical publishers access to removal and replacement information for new types (Art 11). Shredders must require that delivered vehicles are depolluted, have the Art 29 parts removed and come with a copy of the certificate of destruction; they must report non-compliant deliveries (Art 27). Authorised treatment facilities must remove the Annex VIII Part C parts before shredding (Art 29). Sellers of used, remanufactured or refurbished parts must carry the facility's labelling (Art 31). M1/N1 special-purpose vehicles come into scope (Art 2).
  - 14 Aug 2030: plastic recycled in third-country installations counts towards the recycled-content quota only if the installation meets Annex XIII and is audited by a third party at least every five years (Art 6(4)-(5)).
  - 1 Sep 2031: M2, M3, N2, N3, O and L-category vehicles, including special-purpose ones, come into scope (Art 2). Used-vehicle export controls start: only vehicles that are roadworthy on the date the export declaration is lodged may be exported. Customs check each VIN electronically against national registers and refuse release on mismatch (Arts 39-44).
  - 1 Sep 2032 (new types approved from this date): at least 15 % post-consumer recycled plastic, of which at least 20 % must come from end-of-life vehicles or parts removed in use (Art 6(1)-(2)). New types must meet the reusability, recyclability and recoverability rates (Art 4) and must not contain lead, mercury, cadmium or hexavalent chromium, subject to the Annex IV derogations (Art 5(4)-(5)). They must be designed so that listed parts, EV batteries and e-drive motors can be removed (Art 7). Every vehicle placed on the market from this date needs a Digital Circularity Vehicle Passport (Art 13).
  - 1 Sep 2036: 25 % recycled plastic for new types (Art 6(1)).
  - Recycled-content declaration per new type from the first day of the month 12 months after the Art 6 methodology is adopted, due by 31 Aug 2028 (Art 10, Art 6(5)).
- Dedup: grep of data/signals for '2026/1738', 'end-of-life vehicle', 'vrakovišt', 'autovrak' found no ELV record. The one 'end-of-life' hit is reg-plan2026-eu-infringement, which is unrelated. The other EPR records (reg-uwwtd-epr, reg-textiles-epr, packaging) are different instruments.
- Who must act: vehicle manufacturers and importers (EPR, circularity strategy, information access, recycled content, passport), including importers of used vehicles; authorised treatment facilities and shredders; used-parts traders; used-car dealers and platforms (Art 36); used-vehicle exporters (Art 39); producer responsibility organisations. Supervision sits with Member State competent authorities (Arts 14 and 38).
